items.title: Piaget underestimated young children's abilities
items.claim: Piaget's three-mountains task (1956) found children under 7 are 'egocentric' — unable to take another's perspective. What did later work show?

options.text: Piaget's stages are timed exactly correctly

When the task is made more naturalistic (Hughes's policeman doll task, 1975), 3-4 year olds succeed; Piaget's task underestimated perspective-taking ability. False-belief tasks (Wimmer & Perner 1983) reveal more nuanced developmental trajectories

items.reveal:
Martin Hughes's 1975 'naughty boy hiding from policeman' task gave familiar context: ~90% of 3-4 year olds succeeded. Theory of mind (false belief) emerges around age 4; precursors are present earlier in non-verbal tasks (Onishi & Baillargeon 2005).

Piaget's broader staircase model — distinct, age-defined stages with sharp transitions — has been replaced by more gradualist accounts in modern developmental cognitive neuroscience.
items.why: Famous developmental milestones can shift dramatically with task design. Children often know more than the original tasks could reveal.

items.title: Eyewitness memories can be planted
items.claim: Elizabeth Loftus's lab implanted entirely false childhood memories in adult participants. What proportion came to believe the fake event was real?
items.reveal_title: About a quarter of people 'remembered' something that never happened
items.reveal:
In the 'Lost in the Mall' study (Loftus & Pickrell, 1995), 25% of participants came to recall a fabricated childhood event after being told by a family member it had occurred.

Later work with more vivid scenarios reached implantation rates around 50%.
items.why: Memory feels like recording. It is reconstruction, and reconstruction is suggestible.

items.title: The multi-store model was too simple for working memory
items.claim: Atkinson and Shiffrin's 1968 multi-store model split memory into sensory, short-term and long-term stores. What replaced its account of short-term memory?

options.text: Nothing — the multi-store model is unchanged

Baddeley and Hitch's 1974 working memory model — a central executive coordinating a phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad and (later) episodic buffer — better fitted evidence that STM is not a single unitary store

items.reveal:
Patients with impaired STM (e.g., KF, studied by Shallice and Warrington 1970) could nonetheless retain visual information and form new long-term memories — evidence STM had components. Baddeley and Hitch (1974) proposed a multi-component working memory. The episodic buffer was added by Baddeley in 2000.

The multi-store model is still taught as a stepping stone but is superseded for STM specifically.
items.why: Models that fit the original data often fail later, more specific data. Working memory's multiple components matter for education, clinical assessment and cognitive neuroscience.
